executive_summary: SGD/CHF trades at 0.63737 as of the 2026-09-03 close from the gated price store, two sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date, and the pair has risen 1.18 per cent over one month, 2.91 per cent over three, 4.14 per cent over six and 3.59 per cent over twelve — a Singapore dollar that has strengthened against the franc on every horizon measured. Spot sits at the 94th percentile of its 52-week closing range, 22 pips below the closing high of 0.63957 set on 2 September and 318 pips above the closing low of 0.60555, with the daily moving averages stacked bullishly at 50-day 0.6303, 100-day 0.62355 and 200-day 0.61952 and a clean sequence of higher highs and higher lows since March. The dominant bilateral narrative is a policy differential that is both unusually wide and structurally incapable of compressing from the quote side: plus 140.3 basis points of money-market carry, the largest positive carry the Singapore dollar earns anywhere in its benchmarking set, against a Swiss National Bank policy rate of exactly 0.00 per cent conditioned there through 2028, while the Monetary Authority of Singapore has tightened the appreciation slope of its policy band at two consecutive reviews and may do so again on 14 October. Three bilateral differentials diverge materially from what either standalone dossier would suggest. First, the reaction functions are explicitly opposed — one central bank appreciates its currency as policy while the other caps its currency as policy — which is worth more than the rate gap a carry model would price. Second, the IMF DOTS bilateral goods balance is a 5.8 billion dollar structural Singapore deficit dominated by Swiss gold and pharmaceutical shipments, a persistent franc-buying flow that neither dossier scores. Third, the pair's dominant structural obstacle is a 200-week average at 0.64976 that has not been closed above in 118 weeks but is declining at 3.6 pips a week, so it converges on a rising spot inside the strategic window and falls to roughly 0.6405 by end-February 2027. The settled stance is Bullish on both horizons at conviction 3, tactical net weighted score plus 0.4121 and strategic plus 0.3776, and the price payload corroborates rather than contradicts it. The caveat is that fresh post-dossier Swiss data has begun to pull forward first-hike expectations, and if the franc stops being a funding currency the single largest input to this call erodes from the quote side.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The bilateral carry is plus 140.3 basis points annualised in the pair's favour, computed as SORA at 1.4028 per cent (a money-market proxy since MAS operates no policy rate) minus the SNB policy rate of exactly 0.00 per cent. It is the largest positive carry the Singapore dollar earns against any currency in its benchmarking set; the only other positive is the yen at plus 40.3bp. In pip terms, 140.3bp is 89.4 pips a year, 7.45 pips a month and 44.7 pips over six months on a spot of 0.63737. The carry-to-vol ratio cannot be quoted on the framework's preferred implied-vol basis because the pair has no options market; against 60-day realised of 4.96% the ratio is plus 0.283, the best realised carry-to-volatility ratio in the entire Singapore dollar complex, though it is not comparable with implied-vol ratios quoted elsewhere. The regime is working and is sustained by compressed global volatility (VIX 14.4-14.5, US high-yield 260-263bp) which is precisely the environment in which a zero-rate franc is borrowed; a Swiss Bankers Association survey found all bankers expecting the SNB to hold at 0% by year-end with the first hike anticipated June 2027. The regime breaks on a volatility spike, because the franc's payoff to a risk shock is convex and the Singapore dollar's is linear.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral money-market differential is +140.3bp in Singapore's favour — SORA at 1.4028 per cent against an SNB policy rate of exactly 0.00 per cent — and it is the largest positive carry the Singapore dollar earns against any currency in its benchmarking set, with only the yen at +40.3bp also positive. Direction of travel reinforces the level rather than eroding it. MAS steepened the appreciation slope of the S$NEER band at two consecutive reviews, on 14 April and again on 27 July 2026, and the base dossier carries a 55 per cent probability of a third steepening; the SNB, by contrast, has conditioned its entire three-year conditional inflation forecast on the policy rate remaining at zero through 2028 and cannot narrow the gap from its own side without returning to negative rates, which Chairman Schlegel has repeatedly dismissed. Transmission runs through two distinct channels: carry accrual of roughly 7.4 pips a month, and the band's mechanical trade-weighted appreciation of about 10bp a month — of which only a fraction reaches the CHF leg, because the S$NEER is trade-weighted and Switzerland is a small component of Singapore's basket. That partial transmission is the honest limit on tactical conviction. The one dated policy event inside the four-week window is the SNB assessment on 24 September, a quarterly round with a refreshed conditional inflation forecast; a hold at zero is effectively certain, so the tradeable content is entirely in whether the intervention language survives.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential is more likely to widen than to narrow, and the widening comes entirely from the base leg. MAS's revealed reaction function is forward-looking to an unusual degree — it tightened in April before the imported-energy shock appeared in the data and again in July while the most recent core print had eased to 1.6 per cent — and every subsequent datum has validated it, with core inflation at 2.0 per cent, headline at 2.2 per cent, the domestic supply price index at plus 33.4 per cent year on year and the 2026 growth forecast lifted from 2.0-4.0 to 4.5-5.5 per cent. Compounded over six months, a 1.25 to 1.50 per cent slope delivers 60 to 75bp of trade-weighted Singapore dollar appreciation. On the Swiss side there is no mechanism at all: headline CPI is 0.4 per cent, core 0.3 per cent, the conditional forecast runs 0.6, 0.6 and 0.7 per cent for 2026 to 2028, and the two scheduled assessments in the window are both hold-with-forecast rounds. The residual risk to the base leg is Goldman Sachs's published view that a 1.25 per cent slope is already mildly restrictive and that MAS is finished for 2026; CIMB Securities expects a further 25bp of slope in October. That split is unusually wide and is why confidence sits at 70 rather than higher. The strategic risk to the quote leg runs the other way: a return to negative Swiss rates would widen the differential further, so both tails on the Swiss side favour the pair.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both economies are surprising to the upside simultaneously, which is unusual, but only one of them converts the surprise into currency policy. Singapore's Q2 GDP was revised to plus 5.9 per cent year on year and plus 1.4 per cent quarter on quarter, MTI lifted the full-year forecast from 2.0-4.0 to 4.5-5.5 per cent on 11 August, the SIPMM manufacturing PMI printed 51.4 with electronics at 52.4, and unemployment is 2.0 per cent — the lowest in the comparison set. Switzerland has had its own best data run in years: SECO's Q2 flash was plus 1.5 per cent quarter on quarter against a 0.2-0.4 per cent consensus, the KOF barometer hit 106.7, and industrial production ran plus 5.5 per cent against a minus 4.7 per cent forecast. The differential that matters is the inflation one, and it is enormous: MAS core at 2.0 per cent and accelerating against Swiss core at 0.3 per cent, a gap of roughly 170bp. In Singapore, higher inflation and a widening output gap mechanically buy a steeper currency appreciation path because the exchange rate is the instrument. In Switzerland, better growth buys nothing at all, because 0.3 per cent core inflation leaves the SNB pinned. The asymmetry of transmission, not the level of activity, is what makes this factor bullish for the pair. The dated tests inside the window are the Swiss August CPI and detailed Q2 GDP on 3 September and Singapore's August CPI on 23 September.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both growth stories deteriorate at the second derivative, and the question is which deteriorates faster and whether either changes policy. Singapore's electronics engine is decelerating hard — semiconductor output growth fell from plus 37.0 per cent in May to plus 20.8 per cent in June to plus 8.0 per cent in July, and non-electronics NODX is already contracting at minus 2.3 per cent with pharmaceuticals down 56.7 per cent — so the export base is narrow and base effects turn adverse from Q4. Switzerland's problem is more specific and more dateable: the Q2 surge and record July trade surplus are substantially pharmaceutical front-running ahead of US Section 232 tariffs effective 31 July, with chemical and pharmaceutical exports up 25.7 per cent in a single month, so the payback lands inside the strategic window. The inflation differential is the durable part and it stays wide: MAS guides core to remain elevated until moderating from around mid-2027, while the SNB forecasts 0.6 per cent for both 2026 and 2027. A persistent 150-200bp inflation gap between an economy whose central bank responds by appreciating the currency and one whose central bank cannot respond at all is a slow, structural bid for the pair. Confidence falls from 62 to 58 because both growth impulses are borrowed rather than trend, and the weight halves from 0.18 to 0.10 accordingly.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a haven-versus-haven pair, which sounds neutral and is not. The franc is the global haven and, critically, the global funding currency at 0.00 per cent; the Singapore dollar is a regional haven that pays 140bp more and carries a mechanically appreciating policy band. In the current tape — VIX at 14.4 to 14.5, down more than six points over a month, US high-yield at 260 to 263bp and 21 to 27bp tighter, investment grade at 79bp, equity indices near highs — neither currency gets a haven bid, so the differentiating factor is the funding role, and the franc carries it. The cross-sectional evidence in the quote dossier is unambiguous: the franc sits at the weak end of its ranges against the entire high-carry bloc while the Singapore dollar's own risk beta is modest and runs through trade rather than portfolio flows. The one genuine contradiction is gold, up 8.60 per cent over a month and 22.39 per cent over a year: the franc's traditional correlate is being bought hard while the franc is sold, which is read as haven demand rotating into bullion rather than disappearing — a warning about durability rather than direction. Net over four weeks, a benign tape penalises the zero-rate leg more than the positive-carry leg, and that is Bullish for the pair.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk factor stops being a level read and becomes a distribution read, and for this specific pair the distribution is genuinely two-sided. Volatility and credit are close to the tight end of their post-2022 ranges, so there is far more room to widen than to compress, and the strategic calendar is dense with dated binary risk: the US-China tariff truce expiry on 10 November, US midterms on 3 November, Taiwan local elections on 28 November and a US funding cliff on 11 December. In a global risk-off both currencies rally against the dollar, but the franc's payoff is convex and the Singapore dollar's is not — the franc is the closest liquid hedge to European credit stress and the beneficiary of a carry unwind, while the Singapore dollar's regional haven bid works against Asian peers rather than against the franc. Cutting the other way, the SNB has explicitly and asymmetrically committed to lean against rapid franc appreciation, which truncates the right tail of any franc rally, and Singapore's structural inflows are being actively institutionalised through the August asset-management package. A convex quote leg with an official cap against a steadier base leg with a policy floor nets to genuinely no directional signal, and Neutral is the honest reading rather than a refusal to choose.

Neutral is the correct reading, and the low confidence reflects that half the inputs do not exist.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the positioning read flips against the pair, and it does so for a structural reason rather than a tactical one. The franc's remaining short is concentrated in real money — minus 38,322 asset-manager contracts against total open interest of only 109,874, roughly 5.92 billion dollars of notional — and real-money shorts build slowly and unwind violently. Against a strategic window containing an unresolved Middle East conflict, a euro area being tightened into an energy shock and a Fed whose next move is genuinely two-sided, the probability of at least one event forcing that book to cover is materially above zero, and every contract covered is a franc bought, which is a fall in SGD/CHF. On the base leg the offsetting flow is real but slower and bounded: Singapore's structural inflows through corporate treasury relocation, family-office formation and MAS's 19 August asset-management package are persistent rather than cyclical, and the absence of any leveraged futures book means there is no squeeze mechanism on the Singapore dollar side at all. But the base leg also has less room: at roughly 1.7 per cent above the estimated band midpoint the market is already close to where MAS has said it will curb excessive S$NEER volatility. A capped base leg against a squeeze-prone quote leg is a mildly negative strategic positioning signal for the pair. Confidence is only 42 because the trigger is exogenous and undated and because half the inputs are structurally missing.

The dampener that did not exist then is the SNB's current stated willingness to intervene backed by CHF 889.6bn of reserve assets, which caps magnitude without changing direction.
strategic.contrarian_case: The strategic contrarian trade against this pair is to own the franc, not the Singapore dollar. It is the only leg with a concentrated, identifiable, slow-moving short to squeeze, its payoff to a risk event is convex where the Singapore dollar's is linear, and no options market exists in which anyone is being charged for that convexity in this cross. Against that, MAS's structural inflows and the band's mechanical grind are the reason the stance is only mildly Bearish at 42 confidence rather than strongly so.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a surplus-versus-surplus pair and over four weeks the two surpluses cancel. Singapore runs a current account of 16.7 per cent of GDP, the largest in its comparison set; Switzerland runs 9.77 per cent, the second largest in its own. The differential of roughly seven percentage points favours the base leg but is a slow-moving stock-flow variable with no four-week information content. What does move inside four weeks is the terms of trade, and there the balance is adverse for the base leg: Singapore is a net crude importer with a 2025 mineral-fuels trade deficit of 24.7 billion dollars, its terms-of-trade index has fallen to 97.84 from 98.66 and its domestic supply price index is running at plus 33.4 per cent year on year, while Switzerland is a smaller and less exposed net energy importer that benefited from the same Brent decline. The bilateral relationship is small but is a structural flow against the pair: IMF DOTS shows Singapore importing 8.1 billion dollars of goods from Switzerland against 2.2 billion dollars of exports, a net Singapore deficit of 5.8 billion dollars in 2024, dominated by Swiss gold and pharmaceutical shipments. That flow is franc-buying and Singapore-dollar-selling at the margin. Netting a larger base-leg surplus against an adverse base-leg terms-of-trade shock and an adverse bilateral goods balance gives Neutral, and the 0.06 tactical weight means little turns on it.

The bilateral goods deficit is too small to trade and the terms-of-trade deterioration on the base leg is masked by spectacular headline export numbers, so there is no tactical edge here at all.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 strategic weight this becomes the second-largest factor in the framework, and the surplus differential finally dominates the price shock. Singapore's 16.7 per cent-of-GDP current account is not cyclical — it has averaged 12.84 per cent since 1980 and is absorbed partly through reserve accumulation of SGD 33.8bn over twelve months and partly through the persistent real appreciation the S$NEER band institutionalises. Switzerland's 9.77 per cent is also structural, generated by a goods surplus in pharmaceuticals and precision engineering, a financial-services surplus and a primary income stream from a CHF 974bn net international investment position. The differential is therefore genuine but narrower than the raw gap suggests, and two Swiss-specific offsets shrink it further from the franc's side: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs of up to 15 per cent hitting close to half of Swiss goods exports to the United States, and a Swiss commitment to facilitate at least 200 billion dollars of US investment over five years, 67 billion in 2026, with no Singaporean equivalent. Singapore's own offsets are the narrowing export base — three product lines carrying a 24.2 per cent NODX headline while pharmaceuticals fall 56.7 per cent — and the 22.0 per cent of goods exports going to Greater China ahead of the 10 November tariff-truce expiry. On balance the base leg's larger surplus, institutionally recycled into currency appreciation, outruns a franc surplus being actively drained by tariffs and outbound investment commitments.

strategic.what_is_priced: The market prices both surpluses as permanent features and neither as a constraint. What is under-priced is the asymmetry of the offsets: the Swiss surplus faces a dated tariff regime and a large committed outbound investment flow, while Singapore's faces only a cyclical narrowing of its export base.

factors.horizon_split: The stance moves from Neutral to Bullish as the weight rises from 0.06 to 0.16, and the mechanism changes with it. Tactically the surplus differential contains no four-week information and is cancelled by an adverse base-leg terms-of-trade shock and a 5.8 billion dollar bilateral goods deficit. Strategically the cumulative balance-of-payments flow becomes the binding influence: a seven-point-of-GDP surplus differential, recycled through reserve accumulation and an institutionally appreciating band on one side, against a franc surplus being drained by pharmaceutical tariffs and a 200 billion dollar outbound investment commitment on the other.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: Singapore is a net crude importer and refined-product exporter with a 2025 mineral-fuels trade deficit of 24.7 billion dollars and processed petroleum oils as its second-largest export at 51.5 billion dollars; also a large LNG importer. Oil up is unambiguously negative for the Singapore dollar through the import bill, though it is simultaneously the reason MAS is tightening, which partially offsets at longer horizons.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Switzerland is a net energy importer with no domestic production, so oil and natural gas up are mildly negative for the franc, and it is the world's largest gold refining hub with a strong haven correlation to bullion. Gold up is positive for the franc. Gold is also the dominant single line in the bilateral trade relationship with Singapore.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: minus for the base leg (net crude importer, mineral-fuels deficit 24.7bn dollars, terms-of-trade index falling to 97.84) and minus but smaller for the quote leg (lower energy intensity of GDP, no petrochemical export complex). Net effect: mildly bearish SGD/CHF, because the base leg carries the larger negative. Gold up: neutral for the base leg and clearly positive for the quote leg through both the refining channel and the shared haven correlation. Net effect: bearish SGD/CHF, and this is the larger of the two channels because gold has moved 22.39% over twelve months against Brent's much smaller net change. LNG up: strongly negative for the base leg and mildly negative for the quote leg. Net effect: bearish SGD/CHF. Combining, the pair's aggregate commodity beta is modestly negative — a broad commodity rally hurts SGD/CHF more than it helps it — which is one of the two reasons the tactical external-balance stance is Neutral despite the base leg running the larger current-account surplus.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from roughly 88 to 97 dollars. The base leg takes the larger hit: Singapore's import bill and domestic supply price index deteriorate immediately and the terms-of-trade index falls further, while Switzerland's energy import cost rises by less relative to GDP. Estimated net effect approximately minus 0.3 to minus 0.5% on SGD/CHF at the four-week horizon, or 19-32 pips. At the six-month horizon the sign is ambiguous because sustained oil above 95 dollars raises the probability of a further MAS band steepening, bullish through the policy channel.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent from roughly 88 to 79 dollars. Both legs gain on the import bill, the base leg by more, so the immediate net effect is mildly bullish SGD/CHF at perhaps plus 0.2 to plus 0.4%, or 13-25 pips. Over six months the effect inverts, because falling energy removes the imported-inflation impulse driving MAS to tighten and takes an October steepening off the table.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Gold. It is the only commodity with a first-order, same-direction effect on both the quote leg's currency and the bilateral trade balance and it has moved far more than energy over the past year at plus 22.39%. Switzerland still refines close to 70% of newly mined gold, and Switzerland, Australia and Japan were the leading suppliers of gold to Singapore, together 51% of total import value. A continued bullion rally is franc-supportive and bearish for SGD/CHF, a genuine under-appreciated hedge against the pair's bullish carry case. MAS beginning central bank vaulting for foreign governments in October 2026 is a slow structural positive for the base leg, cutting the other way over longer horizons.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Raised 0.02 on both horizons from the 0.07 and 0.12 defaults. Neither central bank in this pair conducts policy primarily through an interest rate — MAS has none and the SNB is at zero — so both reaction functions are communicated rather than priced, and the guidance channel carries an unusually large share of the policy signal.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the cleanest factor in the pair because the two central banks are guiding in opposite directions and both directions favour SGD/CHF rising. MAS's July statement is explicit and cumulative: it will increase the rate of appreciation of the policy band very slightly, with no change to width or centre, building on April's move to cap inflationary pressures. Managing Director Chia Der Jiun said on 28 July that the April move placed policy in a favourable position heading into a stronger inflationary environment and that the positive output gap is now expected to widen rather than narrow. That is a central bank telling the market it intends to appreciate its currency. The SNB's guidance is the mirror image and is deliberately one-sided: on 18 June it stated an increased willingness to intervene to counter rapid and excessive appreciation of the franc, reaffirmed by Chairman Schlegel on 8 July. There is no corresponding commitment to lean against franc weakness, and no plausible level of depreciation at which a bank forecasting 0.6% inflation would object. So the base leg's central bank is committed to making its currency stronger and the quote leg's is committed to preventing its currency from becoming stronger. Credibility on both sides is exceptional — MAS has run the band since 1981 with no successful market challenge, and the SNB has CHF 889.6bn of reserve assets behind its threat. The tactical limitation is that MAS says nothing before 14 October, so the only refresh inside the window is the SNB assessment on 24 September.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices the SNB's intervention language as a permanent feature of the landscape and prices MAS as probably finished after two moves. Both are consensus and neither is fully correct — the tail risk that the SNB softens its language on 24 September is unpriced and is the single largest tactical threat to this factor.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.14 strategic weight this becomes the second-largest factor and it strengthens, because the horizon contains the communication events the tactical window lacks. On the base leg, 14 October brings the Monetary Policy Statement, the Macroeconomic Review and the Q3 advance GDP estimate together, the densest information event in the Singapore calendar; applying MAS's revealed reaction function to core inflation at 2.0% and accelerating, a growth forecast lifted to 4.5-5.5% and an output gap forecast to widen produces a clear bias toward a third move, put at 55% by the base dossier. On the quote leg, the gated calendar carries assessments on 24 September and 10 December, both quarterly rounds with refreshed conditional forecasts, at which the policy rate is effectively certain to stay at zero and the only live variable is the intervention sentence. The SNB's structural incentive to prefer a softer franc is if anything strengthened by the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff, raising its sensitivity to competitiveness loss through the exchange rate. The genuine strategic risk is that both guidance stances go quiet: MAS holding in October would remove the base-leg impulse, and a franc weak enough that intervention is unnecessary would make the SNB's cap non-binding. Confidence at 72 rather than higher reflects the unusually wide published analyst split on the October MAS decision.

strategic.what_is_priced: Consensus prices a MAS that is mildly restrictive and finished and an SNB that tolerates franc weakness indefinitely. We agree on the SNB and diverge on MAS by roughly 15-20 percentage points of probability on the October decision, the cleanest single expression of disagreement with consensus in this pair.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Bullish and confidence rises two points strategically while the weight rises from 0.09 to 0.14. Tactically the guidance is hawkish on the base leg and one-sidedly dovish on the quote leg but static — MAS has said nothing on exchange-rate policy since 28 July and will say nothing before October, so the only refresh is the SNB assessment on 24 September, which carries genuine two-sided risk if the intervention language is softened. Strategically the window acquires the base leg's densest information event on 14 October plus a second Swiss assessment on 10 December, so the factor gains dated catalysts with an estimable reaction function on both sides.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk is the factor where the asymmetry runs against this pair, and it runs against it on both legs for the same reason: shocks that matter are risk-off shocks, and the franc is the convex leg. The dated Swiss item inside the window is the 27 September federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality, which August polling puts at 62% against and 36% in favour, so rejection is the strong base case and the modal outcome is a non-event; passage would be genuinely two-sided for the franc. The undated item is the Middle East, where shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been severely constrained since late February, the US-Iran memorandum expired on 17 August with no successor, and Brent rebounded to roughly 93 dollars by 31 August. That is a direct terms-of-trade hit to the base leg and a haven bid for the quote leg simultaneously — the worst combination for SGD/CHF. Singapore's domestic political risk is negligible and Switzerland's is close to it, so this factor is entirely about external shocks and the differential exposure to them. Singapore is the most trade-dependent large economy in the comparison set with total merchandise trade running at plus 38.6% year on year, meaning any global trade disruption transmits to the base leg faster and harder than to the quote leg. Bearish, but at only 50 confidence and a 0.05 weight, because the probability-weighted expectation is small.

tactical.what_is_priced: Nothing measurable is priced for either leg, because there is no options market for SGD/CHF and no event premium visible in the Swiss vol term structure either. A four-week window containing a referendum, an FOMC and an unresolved energy conflict is being carried for free.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the event set broadens and the asymmetry persists in the same direction. The dense cluster falls in November and December and it is overwhelmingly a base-leg exposure: the US-China tariff truce expires on 10 November with China's reciprocal truce on 19 November and the exclusion process on 31 December, US midterms fall on 3 November, Taiwan holds local elections on 28 November and the US funding cliff arrives on 11 December. Singapore sends 22.0% of its goods exports to Greater China and 9.6% to the United States, so a truce failure hits both ends of its entrepot function at once, and its export boom is now concentrated in exactly the integrated-circuit and disk-media lines most exposed to a Taiwan disruption. The quote leg's strategic items are slower and smaller: Bilaterals III ratification is a multi-year parliamentary process with majority stakeholder support, and the concentration of the Swiss banking system in a single institution is a real but undated tail. Working partially against the bearish read, Singapore's regional safe-haven property is genuine and MAS is institutionalising it through the August asset-management package, and any Asian stress event drives capital into Singapore. But that flow strengthens the Singapore dollar against Asian peers, not against a franc that would be rallying globally on the same news. Net mildly Bearish at low confidence.

strategic.what_is_priced: A VIX of 14.5 and a high-yield spread of 263bp price essentially none of a calendar containing four dated binary events in six weeks. That is a variance mispricing, and in this pair it resolves against the base leg because the base leg is the trade-exposed one and the quote leg is the convex one.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Bearish and the two-point confidence gap reflects composition rather than direction. Tactically the risk is concentrated in one largely non-event referendum on the quote leg plus an unpriced energy tail that hurts the base leg's terms of trade while bidding the quote leg. Strategically it fragments across six dated political and trade events between 3 November and 31 December, none individually dominant, almost all pointing at Singapore's trade channel, and partly offset by the regional safe-haven flow those same events would generate into Singapore.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the rare pair in which both legs are top-tier sovereigns, and the honest bilateral answer is that the differential is immaterial. Singapore is rated Aaa by Moody's and AAA by S&P, both stable, runs an FY2026 budget surplus of SGD 8.5bn or roughly 1.0% of GDP, and is a substantial net creditor despite a headline gross debt figure of 171.3% of GDP that reflects securities issued for investment under the Government Securities Act rather than to fund deficits, with GIC and Temasek together holding roughly 1.34 trillion dollars against a GDP near 560 billion. Switzerland is rated AAA by every major agency, reconfirmed AAA stable by Morningstar DBRS on 16 January 2026, carries general government debt of 37.6% of GDP on the rating-agency measure, runs a fiscal surplus of roughly 0.4% of GDP and is constrained by a constitutional debt brake. Neither sovereign has a bond-supply story, a rating watch or a quotable CDS level, which is itself the finding. On the marginal comparison Singapore edges it on surplus size and on sovereign wealth relative to GDP, but the gap is not large enough to generate a currency signal at any horizon, and nothing inside four weeks changes it.

tactical.what_is_priced: Both sovereigns are priced as exactly what they are, and there is no instrument in this pair in which to express a differentiated view. The only latent mispricing is the recurring misreading of Singapore's 171.3% gross debt figure, which has never produced a market move.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the weight rises from 0.04 to 0.07 and the character of the factor changes from absolute to relative, but in this specific pair the relative comparison is between two of the strongest sovereigns in the world and still produces no differential. The mechanism by which fiscal quality becomes an FX factor is that reserve managers and long-horizon allocators respond to relative quality as peer trajectories deteriorate — but that mechanism bids both legs of SGD/CHF simultaneously and roughly equally against the rest of the G10, which is precisely why it cancels here. What the factor does contribute, on both sides, is a floor: Singapore's AAA status and net creditor position are what make a credibly appreciating exchange-rate band fundable at all, and Switzerland's AAA at 37.6% debt-to-GDP is what underwrites a CHF 889.6bn central bank balance sheet without market question. Both floors truncate the downside of their respective currencies, which is why the scenario distribution for this pair is narrower than a comparable emerging-market or twin-deficit cross. The one asymmetry worth noting is that Singapore is deploying fiscal capacity offensively — a proposed fund tax exemption from year of assessment 2027, a Hedge Fund Investment Programme and an ONE Pass track, explicitly framed against Hong Kong — while Switzerland's fiscal capacity is defensive under the debt brake. That is currency-positive for the base leg at the margin and is not enough to move the stance off Neutral.

strategic.what_is_priced: Both sovereigns' quality is fully and permanently priced and there is no expression vehicle in this cross. The genuine content of this factor is not a trade but a constraint: it is why the tail scenarios for SGD/CHF are bounded on both sides rather than open-ended.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral on both horizons with identical confidence, and the alignment is genuine rather than lazy. Both legs are AAA sovereigns with structural surpluses and no supply problem, so the relative-quality mechanism that makes this factor directional in most pairs bids both currencies equally here and cancels. The only thing that changes between horizons is the weight, from 0.04 to 0.07, and a zero contribution multiplied by a larger weight is still zero.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The defining structural fact about SGD/CHF is that it has no derivatives market. No implied volatility exists for any pair touching the Singapore dollar because there is no listed SGD option on any exchange: no SGD options at CME in any product family, no SGD entry in the CVOL index family, and no options on the SGX USD/SGD futures root. There is consequently no implied volatility, no one-year IV percentile, no variance risk premium, no 25-delta risk reversal, no term structure and no event premium to fade for this cross. No forward funding differential is available because SGD has no listed future on CME or Eurex, so even the forward curve has to be inferred from covered interest parity rather than observed. On the volatility that can be measured, the base dossier's derived analytics put SGD/CHF 60-day realised at 4.94%, a moderate-to-low reading consistent with two low-volatility, heavily managed currencies, giving the pair the best realised carry-to-volatility ratio in the entire Singapore dollar complex at plus 0.284. Liquidity is the other structural constraint: this is a thin cross with no natural two-way flow, quoted through the dollar legs rather than directly, so execution and gap risk are materially worse than in either leg's primary pair. Neutral at low confidence is the only honest stance, and the low confidence is a statement about the missing data rather than about the market.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the structural picture does not improve, and the practical consequence is more severe rather than less. Volatility across the horizon is more likely to rise than to fall on both legs: the base leg's 20-day realised has already moved above its 60-day, which in a managed float is one of the few genuine tells that the trade-weighted index is nearing a band edge or a policy review, and the quote leg's realised is running roughly two points above its own implied with a dense event calendar in November and December. But neither observation can be expressed in this cross, because no options exist. That matters strategically in a way it does not tactically: the strategic case for owning SGD/CHF rests on a policy differential with an identifiable convex risk against it — a franc squeeze driven by a minus 38,322 contract real-money short into a risk event — and the natural way to hold a positive-carry position with a convex tail against it is to buy the tail. Here that is impossible in the cross itself and can only be approximated by owning USD/CHF or EUR/CHF optionality separately, which introduces a dollar or euro leg unrelated to the thesis. The structural conclusion is that this factor is informative about the risk profile and unusable for expression, which is exactly the configuration that argues for Neutral and for sizing the directional view down rather than hedging it.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral on both horizons at identical confidence. The missing volatility surface binds equally at four weeks and six months and is the primary reason confidence sits below 50 on each. The only difference is consequential rather than analytical: tactically the absence of options merely removes an expression choice, while strategically it removes the ability to hedge the one identifiable convex risk against the position, which is a reason to size down rather than a reason to change the stance.

expression_assessment.vol_landscape_summary: There is no volatility landscape for this cross to characterise. No listed SGD option exists on any exchange, so SGD/CHF has no implied volatility at any tenor, no risk reversal, no term structure and no variance risk premium; the pair also has no listed future, so its forward curve is a covered-interest-parity inference rather than an observation. The only measurable volatility is realised, at 5.85% over 20 days and 4.96% over 60 from the gated store, low and consistent with two heavily managed currencies whose central banks both compress the centre of the distribution — and the short window now leads the long one, so tension is building.
expression_assessment.directional_expression: Spot or an over-the-counter forward are the only available instruments, and between them spot is materially preferable. A long SGD/CHF forward gives away the positive carry that is the single largest component of the bullish case — roughly 45 pips over six months — because covered interest parity puts the forward below spot by approximately the 140bp differential. Holding the view in spot keeps the carry. Because no options exist, the standard framework of buying convexity when implied volatility is cheap collapses entirely, and position sizing rather than instrument selection becomes the binding constraint. If convexity against the position is required, it has to be bought in the franc's own liquid crosses — where risk reversals recently saw one of the sharpest intraday swings in history — accepting that this imports a euro or dollar leg unrelated to the thesis.
expression_assessment.event_timing_consideration: The gated calendar puts the only scheduled decisions for either leg at 2026-09-24 and 2026-12-10, both SNB quarterly assessments, at which a hold is effectively certain and the tradeable content is whether the intervention language survives. The base leg's decisive event, the MAS review on 14 October, is not on the gated file at all because MAS has no rate decision to schedule; it is taken from the base dossier and flagged. Because no vol term structure exists, there is no event premium to buy before those dates or to sell after them, so there is no timing argument for waiting — the only timing consideration is that the pair's largest scheduled step-change falls in mid-October, inside the strategic window and outside the tactical one, and that the declining 200-week average converges on spot in roughly the same period.
expression_assessment.liquidity_note: A thin cross with no natural two-way corporate flow, quoted and hedged through two separate dollar legs. Bid-offer, slippage and gap risk are all materially worse than in USD/SGD or USD/CHF, and the absence of any listed instrument means there is no exchange-cleared venue for the exposure at all. Any position has to be sized for the worse of the two underlying liquidity profiles rather than the better. The 19 August session — an 83-pip single-day fall, 2.7 times ATR — is the practical illustration.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Reduced 0.04 on both horizons from the 0.11 and 0.12 defaults. tactical.bilateral_analysis: Dollar funding reaches this cross indirectly but not weakly, because both legs settle through the dollar and one of them is the world's funding currency. Conditions are as benign as they get: the three-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis was plus 0.05bp on 1 September with an August range of minus 0.81 to plus 0.71, Federal Reserve central bank liquidity swaps outstanding were 121 million dollars, reserve balances were 2.92 trillion dollars, SOFR printed 3.65 to 3.68 per cent with no month-end dislocation, and the Fed balance sheet is flat rather than contracting. The transmission to the pair is through the carry trade: abundant dollars and compressed volatility keep franc-funded positions alive, and the franc at 0.00 per cent is the leg being borrowed while the Singapore dollar at 1.4028 per cent with an appreciating band is the kind of leg being bought. Covered interest parity is also holding cleanly in the Singapore market — three-month compounded SORA of 1.1805 per cent against a three-month dollar term proxy of 3.64 per cent gives 2.4595 percentage points against a forward-implied 2.4547, agreement to half a basis point — so there is no funding premium distorting either leg's pricing. Singapore's role as an Asian dollar clearing centre with 428 billion dollars of reserves adds a second layer of insulation on the base leg. The offsetting consideration is that a Fed hike on 16 September tightens the marginal cost of dollars, but a hike from a position of ample reserves and a zero basis is a very different event from a hike into scarcity.

tactical.what_is_priced: Funding markets price abundance and are right to. There is no stress to fade and no dislocation to arbitrage in either leg. The tactical positive is simply that the one mechanism that reliably produces a violent franc rally — a global dollar squeeze forcing a carry unwind — is comprehensively absent.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months abundance stops being an observation and becomes an assumption, and two considerations pull the stance back to Neutral. The first is the rate of change in reserves: balances have fallen from 2.99 trillion dollars on 5 August to 2.92 trillion on 26 August, roughly 20 billion a week, and sustained drainage at that pace would remove about 500 billion over the horizon. The second is the calendar: the US funding cliff on 11 December coincides with year-end balance-sheet compression, and 31 December is the single largest recurring dollar-funding squeeze of the year. Basis widening at year-end forces carry positions down, and in this pair the carry position being reduced is short-franc, which is mechanically bearish for SGD/CHF. Against that, the structural positives persist on both legs: Singapore's Asian dollar clearing function is backed by 428 billion dollars of reserves and a zero basis six months into an energy shock is genuine evidence of system resilience, while Switzerland has no dollar funding vulnerability at all. Netting an easy funding backdrop against a deteriorating rate of change and a seasonal year-end squeeze that specifically penalises the position leaves no directional signal.

tactical.score_interpretation: Weights sum to exactly 1.00 and contributions sum to plus 0.4121, which is comfortably beyond the plus 0.10 threshold and therefore Bullish for SGD/CHF — the pair rising, the Singapore dollar strengthening against the franc. The number should be read as breadth rather than depth. Six of ten factors are positive and only one is negative, but no single factor contributes more than 0.169, five factors contribute exactly zero at a combined weight of 0.25, and the largest contributor rests on a carry differential that is fully observable and therefore fully embedded in the pair's covered-interest-parity forward. The gross positive of plus 0.4371 comes from Policy and Rates at plus 0.1690, Inflation and Growth at plus 0.1116, Guidance at plus 0.0630, Risk Appetite at plus 0.0550 and USD Liquidity at plus 0.0385, against a single Event Risk drag of minus 0.0250. Three of those five bullish contributions — rates, risk appetite and dollar funding — are facets of one underlying regime rather than independent evidence, namely that compressed volatility and abundant dollars make a zero-rate franc the funding leg while a positive-carry currency with an appreciating band is the recipient. That correlation is the honest reason conviction is 3 rather than 4 on a score this size: the factors are not as independent as their count suggests, and a single volatility shock would flip three of them at once.
tactical.rationale: Two factors carry 44 per cent of the tactical weight between them and both point the same way, which is why the score is large. Policy and Rates at 0.26 is the dominant input and the differential is unusually clean: plus 140.3bp of money-market carry in Singapore's favour, the largest positive carry the Singapore dollar earns anywhere, against a quote-leg policy rate pinned at exactly 0.00 per cent and conditioned there through 2028. Inflation and Growth at 0.18 adds a second, independent bullish input through an asymmetry of transmission rather than of data — both economies are surprising to the upside, but Singapore's core inflation at 2.0 per cent and its output gap widening convert directly into a steeper currency appreciation path because the exchange rate is the instrument, while Switzerland's plus 1.5 per cent quarter buys nothing at all against 0.3 per cent core. The base and quote dossier views reinforce rather than conflict: the base dossier is Bullish SGD at plus 0.2307 and the quote dossier is Bearish CHF at minus 0.2358, and crossing them naively gives roughly plus 0.47 against our plus 0.4121, so this verdict is slightly more conservative than a mechanical combination of the two standalone views. The bilateral-specific modifiers all cut the same way and all cut against the score: an IMF DOTS bilateral goods balance showing Singapore importing 8.1 billion dollars from Switzerland against 2.2 billion of exports, a 5.8 billion dollar structural franc-buying flow dominated by gold and pharmaceuticals; a gold price up 22.39 per cent over twelve months that is franc-supportive through the refining and haven channels; and a base leg that is the most trade-exposed economy in the comparison set going into a November calendar dense with trade risk. What is priced versus what we expect is the crux and it is uncomfortable. Covered interest parity puts the pair's forward below spot by approximately the carry, so the plus 140bp that is doing most of the work in Factor 1 is already monetised — a long position wins on total return provided spot merely falls by less than the forward discount, but the directional call requires the band's trade-weighted grind to actually reach the CHF leg, and it reaches it only partially because Switzerland is a small component of Singapore's basket. What is genuinely unpriced is a third MAS steepening, because no instrument quotes MAS band decisions. The path of least resistance over four weeks is therefore a slow grind higher rather than a move, with carry accruing at roughly 7.4 pips a month. Dated catalysts inside the window are the SNB assessment on 24 September from the gated calendar, Singapore's August CPI on 23 September, the Swiss GDP and CPI double header on 3 September and the Swiss neutrality referendum on 27 September. Conviction is 3 rather than 4 because three of the five bullish contributions describe a single volatility regime and would flip together, because the pair has no options market in which to hedge the identifiable convex risk against it, and because it is a thin cross with materially worse execution than either leg's primary pair.
tactical.g10_relative_ranking: Among Singapore dollar crosses, long SGD/CHF ranks first on risk-adjusted carry: it is one of only two crosses where the Singapore dollar earns positive carry at all, at plus 140.3bp against plus 40.3bp versus the yen, and it carries the best realised carry-to-volatility ratio in the entire complex at plus 0.284. It ranks behind short NZD/SGD only on the size of the raw fundamental gap. Among franc shorts, SGD/CHF ranks third or fourth: AUD/CHF and NOK/CHF pay 435bp and 425bp against 140bp here, so on raw carry the commodity bloc dominates, but SGD/CHF has by far the highest-quality base leg — a AAA sovereign with the largest current-account surplus in the set and a central bank institutionally committed to appreciating its own currency — and is the only franc short whose base leg has an explicit policy mechanism working for it rather than merely a rate.

The pair has just failed at 0.64004 on 3 September and needs to clear 0.63752 and then the 52-week high at 0.64016 to establish the next leg; with an ATR of 31 pips that is one to two clean sessions of work, but the failure means a retest of the 0.6350-0.6360 shelf in the first week is more likely than an immediate breakout. The middle fortnight should be quiet in absolute terms — 20-day realised of 5.85% implies a 23.5-pip standard daily move — with the pair working into the 0.6439-0.64997 five-touch band around the 23 September Singapore CPI and the 24 September SNB assessment, which are the two dated events capable of producing a 40 to 60 pip move in either direction. The SNB date is the genuinely two-sided one and the market will not extend length meaningfully ahead of it, so expect a pullback of 40 to 60 pips at some point between 10 and 23 September, most plausibly toward 0.6350 and the rising 50-day average now at 0.6303. From there the resolution is mechanical rather than narrative: the declining 200-week average at 0.64976 is falling 3.6 pips a week toward a rising spot, so the confrontation with the pair's dominant multi-year ceiling arrives inside the tactical window on the base-case pace and inside the next two months on almost any path. The risk to this shape is a gap rather than a drift — the 19 August session produced an 83-pip single-day fall on a thin cross with no listed hedge.

strategic.score_interpretation: Weights sum to exactly 1.00 and contributions sum to plus 0.3776, which is Bullish for SGD/CHF under the mechanical threshold. The composition differs materially from the tactical score and is more concentrated in the factors that should matter over quarters: Policy and Rates at plus 0.1820, Guidance at plus 0.1008 and External Balance at plus 0.0880 together supply plus 0.3708 of a gross positive of plus 0.4288, with Inflation and Growth adding plus 0.0580 against drags from Event Risk at minus 0.0260 and Flows at minus 0.0252. Four factors score zero at a combined weight of 0.23, and in each case the zero is a genuine two-sided assessment: risk appetite because a convex quote leg with an official cap balances a steadier base leg with a policy floor, fiscal because both legs are AAA sovereigns and the differential cancels, market structure because no derivatives market exists for the pair, and dollar funding because current abundance is offset by a year-end turn that specifically penalises the position. The strategic score is below the tactical one despite a stronger policy read, and the reason is instructive: the two factors that turn negative or drop out strategically — positioning and dollar funding — are precisely the ones that describe how a long SGD/CHF position gets forced out rather than how it gets proved wrong on fundamentals.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework loads onto Policy and Rates at 0.26, External Balance at 0.16 and Guidance at 0.14, and the Singapore dollar wins all three. Policy wins because MAS has a live path and the SNB has none: compounded over six months a 1.25 to 1.50 per cent band slope delivers 60 to 75bp of trade-weighted Singapore dollar appreciation while the Swiss policy rate is conditioned at zero through 2028 and both scheduled assessments on the gated calendar, 24 September and 10 December, are hold rounds. Guidance wins because the two reaction functions are explicitly opposed and both favour the pair rising — MAS is committed to appreciating its currency and has done so twice pre-emptively, while the SNB has stated an increased willingness to intervene against rapid franc appreciation with no symmetric commitment against weakness. External Balance wins on a seven-percentage-point current-account differential, 16.7 per cent of GDP against 9.77 per cent, with the Swiss surplus additionally drained by Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs and a committed 200 billion dollar outbound US investment programme that has no Singaporean equivalent. The two dossiers interact asymmetrically here: the base dossier is Bullish SGD strategically at plus 0.3904 while the quote dossier is Neutral CHF at minus 0.0499, so unlike the tactical horizon this verdict rests on base-leg strength rather than on quote-leg weakness — the franc is not falling apart, the Singapore dollar is being appreciated by policy. The bilateral modifiers are the honest counterweight and they are the reason the score is not larger. The IMF DOTS bilateral goods balance is a 5.8 billion dollar structural franc-buying flow driven by Swiss gold and pharmaceutical shipments into Singapore; gold up 22.39 per cent over twelve months is franc-supportive through both that trade channel and the haven correlation; the franc carries a concentrated minus 38,322 contract real-money short that is squeeze fuel into a November calendar containing four dated binary events; and the 31 December funding turn mechanically forces exactly this position down. What is priced versus what we expect is the decisive question and the answer is nuanced. Crossing the two dossiers' own six-month dollar forecasts — USD/SGD at 1.2560 and USD/CHF at 0.7950 — gives an implied SGD/CHF of roughly 0.6329, about 0.7 per cent below spot, which is simply the carry showing up as a forward discount rather than a bearish view. Our bullish call is therefore explicitly a call that the pair's spot outperforms its covered-interest-parity forward on the strength of the trade-weighted differential: an appreciating S$NEER against a trade-weighted franc that both dossiers describe as roughly unchanged to weaker. The path of least resistance is a slow grind higher punctuated by one genuine discontinuity on 14 October, when the MAS statement, the Macroeconomic Review and the Q3 advance GDP estimate publish together. Other dated catalysts are the SNB assessments on 24 September and 10 December, the tariff-truce expiry on 10 November, Taiwan's elections on 28 November and the year-end funding turn. Conviction is 3 because the policy mechanism is mechanical rather than discretionary — a band with an appreciating slope delivers currency strength whether or not anyone believes in it — but not higher, because the convex risk sits entirely on the other side of the trade and there is no options market in this cross in which to hedge it.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically, long SGD/CHF ranks first among expressions of a bullish Singapore dollar view on a carry-adjusted basis and second on fundamental gap behind short NZD/SGD, because it is the only Singapore dollar cross with meaningfully positive carry, the best realised carry-to-volatility ratio in the complex at plus 0.284, and a quote-leg central bank explicitly committed to capping its own currency. Among franc shorts it ranks behind AUD/CHF and NOK/CHF on raw carry — 435bp and 425bp against 140bp — but ahead of both on the quality and policy support of the base leg, and comfortably ahead of GBP/CHF and CAD/CHF, where the base leg has a deteriorating external balance and no appreciation mechanism. Against EUR/CHF, the quote dossier's own cleanest short-franc expression, SGD/CHF trades a dated ECB catalyst for a dated MAS one and a euro-area twin-surplus of 1.93 per cent of GDP for a Singaporean one of 16.7 per cent.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic shape is a stepped grind with one genuine discontinuity and one mechanical resolution. Through September the pair should trade the two-sided SNB assessment and the Singapore CPI, ending the month somewhere between 0.6400 and 0.6450 in the base case. The 14 October MAS event is the step: a steepening should carry the pair 60 to 90 pips higher over the following fortnight as the band's implied path resets, taking it into the upper half of the 0.6439-0.64997 band, while a hold should produce a faster 80 to 120 pip decline as the band deviation unwinds — an asymmetry in speed rather than magnitude, because unwinds are quicker than grinds. The mechanical resolution runs in parallel and is independent of the October outcome: the 200-week average declines 3.6 pips a week from 0.64976, so on the base-case appreciation pace of roughly 4 pips a week the two converge in about 16 weeks, in late December 2026, and by end-February the average has fallen to approximately 0.6405 — 31 pips above today's spot. In other words the pair's dominant multi-year ceiling comes to meet it, and the confrontation happens inside the window whatever the price does. November is likely to be the widest stretch of the horizon, containing US midterms on the 3rd, the tariff-truce expiry on the 10th, APEC on the 18th-19th and Taiwan's elections on the 28th, and the realistic expectation there is a chop between 0.6380 and 0.6500 rather than directional progress. The final leg into February should reassert the grind as the January MAS review and Q4 advance GDP reset expectations. Pullback levels on the way up are 0.6400, the 50-day now at 0.6303 and the two-touch shelf at 0.6284; the level that breaks the thesis is a weekly close below 0.61981.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Both horizons are Bullish at conviction 3, with scores of plus 0.4121 tactically and plus 0.3776 strategically — within 0.035 of each other. But the composition changes substantially, and the alignment is therefore genuine rather than a carry-forward. Tactically the score is regime-driven: five of six bullish contributions come from carry, compressed volatility and abundant dollar funding, three expressions of one underlying condition. Strategically the score is policy-driven: Policy, Guidance and External Balance supply plus 0.3708 of the plus 0.4288 gross positive between them, while Risk Appetite and USD Liquidity drop to zero and Flows turns negative. The tactical case is that the franc is currently the funding leg of choice; the strategic case is that the Singapore dollar is being appreciated by its own central bank. Different mechanisms reaching the same direction is a more robust configuration than the same mechanism reaching it twice.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the four-week window as accumulation into the 14 October decision rather than as a trade in its own right. The tactical component is the more fragile of the two because three of its bullish inputs would flip together on a single volatility shock and it has no dated catalyst of its own beyond a Swiss hold. The strategic component has a genuine step-change on 14 October and a mechanical resolution — the declining 200-week average converging on a rising spot in roughly 16 weeks — that does not depend on any narrative at all. Hold the exposure in spot rather than forward so the positive carry is retained rather than surrendered to the forward discount, and size for the absence of any hedge in the cross itself. A caveat: fresh post-dossier Swiss data has begun pulling forward first-hike expectations for the SNB, and the 3 September session's intraday failure at 0.64004 is the first evidence of that mechanism working against the strategic magnitude, though not against the direction.

catalysts.event: Swiss August CPI and detailed Q2 2026 GDP
catalysts.rationale: Both prints land the same morning and both are franc-ambiguous individually but franc-negative jointly for this cross. A soft CPI near 0.0% month on month confirms the SNB is pinned at zero and keeps the 140.3bp carry differential permanent, while a strong GDP revision buys no policy response at 0.3% core inflation. Strong growth that cannot move a policy rate is the definition of a currency that stays a funding leg, which is bullish for SGD/CHF. Observed outcome: both beat, prompting profit-taking in EUR/CHF and USD/CHF though SNB outlook unchanged; the pair failed at 0.64004 intraday and closed 22 pips below the prior day — the event resolved against the label.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with staff projections
catalysts.rationale: A 25bp hike to a 2.50% deposit rate is close to fully priced and would take the euro-franc policy spread from 225bp to 250bp, extending the franc's role as Europe's funding currency. That pressure transmits to SGD/CHF through the quote leg without touching the base leg at all. The tradeable content is the guidance: an explicit signal that the cycle is complete would collapse the euro terminal-rate premium and is the most likely source of a franc rally in September, working against the pair.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: A hike carried at 57 to 68% on third-party citations of CME FedWatch would widen the Singapore money-market disadvantage to the dollar from 222 to about 247bp and lift USD/SGD, while also firming the dollar against the franc. For the cross the two effects largely offset, because both legs are being sold against a stronger dollar. The residual for SGD/CHF runs through the carry regime: a hawkish outcome that keeps volatility compressed sustains franc-funded carry and is marginally bullish for the pair.

catalysts.event: Singapore August CPI and MAS Consumer Price Developments
catalysts.rationale: The most important base-leg data point inside the tactical window and the mechanism by which the market's October probability converges with the base dossier's 55% probability. July core rose to 2.0% on an 8.7% year-on-year jump in electricity and gas as the Q3 regulated tariff passed through, and August has a full month of that tariff rather than a partial one. A core print at or above 2.2% makes an October steepening the base case, and the widened inflation differential against Swiss core at 0.3% transmits directly to the pair.

catalysts.event: SNB monetary policy assessment with refreshed conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: The only scheduled decision for either leg inside the tactical window. A hold at 0.00% is effectively certain, so the entire tradeable content is the language: the June statement's increased willingness to intervene against rapid and excessive franc appreciation was written when the franc was under upward pressure, and after a six-month depreciation against the euro that pressure has abated. Retention of the sentence keeps the quote leg capped and supports the pair; removal or softening would be read as tolerance of a stronger franc and is the single largest scheduled threat to the tactical stance.

This is where the base leg's AI capital-expenditure deceleration is most visible: semiconductor output growth has fallen from plus 37.0% in May to plus 20.8% in June to plus 8.0% in July. A further leg toward zero would undercut the growth forecast that underpins the October tightening case and therefore the pair's principal strategic driver, while stabilisation above plus 5% would confirm that the level of output holds as the growth rate normalises.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality
catalysts.rationale: August polling puts rejection at 62% against 36% in favour, so the modal outcome is a non-event. Passage would bar Switzerland from joining sanctions absent a UN mandate and force a re-examination of the framework under which CHF 8.5bn of Russian-linked assets are frozen, which is genuinely two-sided for the franc — arguably enhancing the neutrality claim that underwrites its haven status while raising secondary-sanctions and market-access friction. With no vol surface on either leg's cross, the roughly 20% passage tail is being carried for free.

catalysts.event: MAS October Monetary Policy Statement, Macroeconomic Review and Q3 advance GDP estimate
catalysts.rationale: The single largest scheduled step-change available to this pair, and all three releases publish together. A further steepening of the S$NEER appreciation slope toward roughly 1.50% a year would raise the mechanical appreciation rate of the base leg's trade-weighted index and reset the range for every Singapore dollar cross, including this one, higher. A hold unwinds the estimated 1.7% band deviation toward the midpoint, and unwinds are faster than grinds. Not on the gated calendar, which carries no SGD entry because MAS has no rate decision to schedule; the date is the base dossier's reading of the SingStat advance release calendar and is flagged.

The quote dossier identifies this as the strategic inflection for the franc: a hold at 2.50% would confirm the euro-area tightening cycle is complete, ending the widening phase of the euro-franc spread that has been the dominant source of franc weakness. That is franc-supportive and therefore a drag on SGD/CHF, though it does not touch the base leg's own appreciation mechanism, so the effect on this cross is second-order rather than decisive.

The reduced rates agreed in November 2025 run to this date, with China's reciprocal truce expiring on 19 November and the exclusion process on 31 December. Singapore sends 22.0% of its goods exports to Greater China and 9.6% to the United States, so a lapse hits both ends of its entrepot function simultaneously and disrupts total merchandise trade running at plus 38.6% year on year. Switzerland's exposure is far smaller and its currency is the convex beneficiary of the risk-off that would accompany a failure, so the event is doubly bearish for the pair.

The base leg's export boom is now concentrated in integrated circuits and disk media, and Taiwan was Singapore's third-largest NODX destination in July at plus 32.4%, so any Taiwan-related market disruption hits Singapore's growth engine directly. The quote leg would receive a haven bid on the same news, capped only by the SNB's stated willingness to intervene. Both legs move against the pair in that scenario, which is why the event is bearish rather than merely volatile.

catalysts.event: SNB monetary policy assessment with refreshed conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: The final Swiss decision inside the strategic window and the second of only two scheduled decisions for either leg on the gated file. A hold at 0.00% is near-certain and the variables are the intervention language and any revision to the 2027 and 2028 conditional forecast path. Retention of the cap sustains the pair's principal quote-leg support; a softening would remove it. A revision of the forecast toward zero would revive the small negative-rate tail, widening the differential further, bullish for the pair. A Swiss Bankers Association survey showed all bankers expecting the SNB to keep its rate at 0% by year-end, so a December hold is close to universal, but August data has begun pulling the first hike forward in market pricing.

catalysts.event: Year-end dollar funding turn and expiry of the US-China tariff exclusion process
catalysts.rationale: The 31 December turn is the largest recurring dollar-funding squeeze in the calendar and the most reliable seasonal source of cross-currency basis widening, from a current three-month EUR/USD basis of plus 0.05bp with considerable room to widen and none to tighten. Basis widening forces franc-funded carry positions to be reduced, and in this pair the position being reduced is precisely a short franc against a positive-carry currency — so the seasonal flow buys the quote leg. The simultaneous tariff-exclusion expiry adds a base-leg trade shock on the same date.

assumptions: Price payload quoted exactly as delivered: dataPoints 130, dateRange 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, spot 0.63737 at spotDate 2026-09-03, computationRange 2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03 (4879 weekday bars). The 130 delivered bars are the recent price-action window; moving averages and support/resistance are computed over the whole 4,879-bar stored history.

Spot date (2026-09-03) precedes nothing and follows the valuation date (2026-09-01) by two sessions. Every level, target and pip calculation is anchored to 0.63737, not the 0.63593 close for 31 August the base dossier carries. The 14-pip difference is disclosed, not reconciled.

Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes; weekend bars never enter the store, so the 200-week average is a genuine 200-week average of weekday closes. The convergence arithmetic divides the 124-pip gap by the average's slope plus an assumed rate of spot appreciation, producing week-count estimates, not price forecasts.

No implied volatility exists for this pair, and this is structural rather than a fetch failure: impliedVol.available is false because Singapore has no listed FX option on any exchange. pair_3m_iv is null throughout, carry-to-volatility is quoted only on a realised basis and flagged as not comparable with implied-vol ratios elsewhere.

Forward points are inferred, not observed: funding.available is false because SGD has no listed future on CME or Eurex. All forward outrights are covered-interest-parity inferences from the +140.3bp money-market differential, carrying no term-structure or cross-currency-basis component; a dealer quote will differ.

Rates block: policyRate and yield10y are null for the base leg by construction (MAS targets the S$NEER band, not a rate); SORA (1.4028%) is used throughout as an explicitly labelled money-market proxy. The quote leg's yield10y (0.31%, series IRLTLT01CHM156N, 2026-06-01) is a monthly series 92 days stale at the valuation date and is used only for directional comparison.

Direction Verdict carried through unchanged: all ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, applied weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, score interpretations, rationales, G10 rankings, contrarian analyses, net commodity exposure and expression assessment are reproduced verbatim from the settled Direction Verdict, scored without the price payload. Nothing was re-scored because the chart agreed or disagreed.

Citation architecture: factor blocks cite the Direction Verdict's own inherited dossier citation set, labelled 'Direction Verdict refs'; the numbered citations are exclusively sources accessed during this pass's bilateral web research. Cache-derived figures (spot, moving averages, realised volatility, ATR, zones, percentiles, performance) carry no external citation by design.

No bank forecast exists for SGD/CHF and none was fabricated. Crossed dollar-leg figures in the consensus section are arithmetic combinations of independently published USD/SGD and USD/CHF forecasts by houses not asked about this cross, labelled as such. Retail extrapolation pages are cited for completeness and not relied upon.

Bilateral trade: the IMF DOTS block was used directly in Factor 5 and the net commodity exposure calculation. It is 2024-vintage goods data, two years old at the valuation date; the compositional inference that Swiss exports to Singapore are dominated by gold and pharmaceuticals is drawn from the dossiers' export-structure descriptions and bilateral web research, not from the DOTS aggregate itself.

Scenario and invalidator probabilities are analyst judgements calibrated to the factor analysis and the pair's realised-volatility distribution, not derived from an options-implied distribution, because none exists for this cross. Scenario probabilities sum to 100% on each horizon.

Weight adjustments total three factors across both horizons, each within the ±0.05 limit, with both schedules summing to exactly 1.00. The reasons are recorded in the Weight Adjustments table and were set by the Direction Verdict, not by this pass.

Liquidity and execution: this is a thin cross with no natural two-way corporate flow, no exchange-cleared venue and no listed hedge, quoted and hedged through two separate dollar legs. Every position-sizing figure already halves the notional a comparable-volatility major would justify.
